channel.title: Turisync
channel.description: Travel tech analysis: AI in travel, distribution, hotel, airline and port tech, startups and funding.

item.title: Nichupté bridge, six months in: an 11.2 km link that reshapes Cancún's airport and hotel-zone traffic
item.description: The bridge over Laguna Nichupté opened May 2, 2026, with three lanes, a cycle path, solar panels and capacity for 12,000 vehicles a day. What it changes for ground transport operators.

item.title: The Mexican Caribbean's AI gap: hotels use chatbots, but few build their own systems
item.description: Only four in ten tourism companies in the region invest in technology, and a local tech director warns guests will notice the AI gap within 24 months. Where the opportunity is.

item.title: Visitax goes digital: what Quintana Roo's shift away from airport collection means for travel platforms
item.description: Quintana Roo plans to end in-person collection of its 293-peso visitor fee at Cancún airport. Hoteliers report demands more than 80% above the fee. The integration opportunity for OTAs and airlines.

item.title: Cancún airport's biometric e-gates: 40 planned, 30 eligible countries and a digital FMM
item.description: Cancún is scaling automated immigration from 26 to 40 e-gates and from 48 to 54 manual booths. Who can use them and why it matters for peak-season throughput.

item.title: The sargassum tech stack: how satellites, ocean models and drones now track the Mexican Caribbean's biggest risk
item.description: NOAA's risk tool went daily at 1 km resolution in 2026, and UNAM reads Sentinel-2 imagery every five days. What the monitoring stack can and cannot do for hotels and tour operators.

item.title: Mexico's first cruise home port: the tech stack a turnaround terminal needs
item.description: Puerto Vallarta will host Mexico's first cruise home port. Turning a port of call into a turnaround terminal is as much a systems project as a construction one. Here's the stack to watch.
